academicJudgment.claimTested: UCR offers genuine regional connections in Arabic and Near Eastern narrative, Islamic Mediterranean artistic exchange and Persian imperial history, supported by substantial comparative political, social, economic and cultural inquiry. Its strongest feasible combinations do not sustain Middle Eastern societies and sources as the continuing object of historical, religious, political-economic, ethnographic and modern literary study. General comparative tools or hypothetical region-focused research do not create that taught regional progression. This is not a judgment based on missing language teaching alone.
academicJudgment.strongestObjection: The selected external MMO route is interdisciplinary and requires only basic regional language. UCR has real Near Eastern/Arabic narrative, Islamic courts, Persian imperial history, global literary/artistic interpretation, decolonial sociology, international conflict and political economy. A LAS programme need not be a disciplinary replica, and available comparative inquiry is substantive. The actual external literature course supports translated-source work, so lack of Arabic alone cannot justify rejection.
academicJudgment.finding: Both nine-advanced full feasible trials give those positives weight and improve the earlier proposal with more literary/film and material-cultural methods. Nonetheless most taught UCR inquiry addresses wider or other regional cases; none of the strengthened programmes sustains Middle Eastern historical change, religious traditions, regional political economy, ethnographic societies and modern national literatures as its continuing academic object. The known external course bodies establish those connections independently of the duplicate, travel, language proficiency or entry dispute. Assigning students hypothetical regional projects cannot manufacture missing taught subject matter. This is a substantive programme-level assessment without a course-count/EC threshold.
academicJudgment.narrowCoreTest: Excluding only language study and the unknown 5 EC leaves a confirmed substantial non-language regional core that still lacks a sustained taught UCR response. Restricting the positive claim to generic research methods/digital humanities would abandon the verified target identity; not a meaningful narrower academic-core comparison.
